raw_answer_text:
I'll create a FigDown topology figure showing the branch office WAN uplinks structure with the nodes and connections you specified.

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

node access1 "Access Switch 1"
node access2 "Access Switch 2"
node branch "Branch Router"
node hubprimary "Regional Hub"
node hubbackup "Regional Hub"

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary class=primary
edge branch hubbackup class=backup

class primary "Primary WAN Link"
class backup "Backup WAN Link"
```

This topology document declares:

- **Five nodes** representing the network equipment: two access switches, a branch router, and two regional hub routers
- **Four edges** showing the connections: both access switches connect to the branch router, and the branch router connects to both regional hubs
- **Two classes** that give semantic meaning to the two WAN links—distinguishing the primary path from the redundant backup path

The rendering will show these nodes positioned logically with the access switches on the left, the branch router in the center, and the two regional hubs on the right, with edges between them clearly showing the uplink topology.
